titulo: Your prompt generator: from storyboard to prompt list with an agent
lead: Writing eight prompts by hand, with the same look and the same lock, is tiring and leaves room for mistakes. An AI assistant with clear rules drafts the whole list from the storyboard in course 0. You review it, the page checks it, and the list goes to any generator.
objetivo: turn the storyboard from course 0 into a prompt list, one per shot, with an AI assistant, and check it on the page.

aprende.t: Why let an AI assistant draft the list
The request in six layers: role, input, output, vocabulary, rules and limits
Review what the assistant made up before you generate
Put everything the course produced into a plan with dates

nos.detalhe: storyboard.txt (course 0, lesson 8), lookbook.txt (lesson 3) and referencias.txt (lesson 5). All in text, in the project folder.
Role, input, output format, vocabulary, rules and limits. This is what makes the assistant always return the same format.
The top model in your AI subscription, in the chat you already use. No terminal or program needed.
One line per shot: number, duration, size, movement, prompt and sound. Header with the base prompt and the lock.
The page checks format, movement, sound and the total of seconds. You check whether the assistant made up a character, place or object.
Each line becomes one generation, in the generator you chose in lesson 1. The list stays in the folder: switch generators without redoing it.

secoes.legenda: The assistant speeds up the draft; the direction is still yours. Every line passes through your eyes before you spend credits.

secoes.sub: The example turns the 30-second storyboard of "The first batch" into a list.

texto: Eight shots call for eight prompts with the same base prompt and the same lock, word for word. By hand, one forgotten comma changes the look of a shot.
A request with fixed rules makes the assistant repeat what has to stay the same and change only what changes. You swap the storyboard and reuse the request.

passos.titulo: The six layers of the request
texto: Role (who it is), input (the pasted files), output format (the exact line), vocabulary (the camera terms from course 0), rules (copy the base prompt and lock, sound in a separate sentence) and limits (what to do when information is missing).
The limits layer is the one that protects you most: instead of making things up, the assistant writes "FALTA:" and what was missing.
The page checks format and numbers. You read looking for what wasn't in the storyboard: an extra character, a new object, a swapped line of dialogue.
Found something made up? Don't just fix the line: add the missing rule to the request, so it doesn't come back with the next storyboard.
To generate, paste the base prompt, the lock, and the shot line, and attach the references for that shot. If the generator wants a different way of writing, adjust the line, not the list.
The list, the storyboard, the lookbook, and the references stay in the folder. If the generator changes or shuts down, you take everything to another one.

secoes.titulo: The layered request and the list format
secoes.sub: Paste the request into your AI assistant's chat from your subscription, with the three files at the end.

blocos.rot: Request to the AI assistant (prompt writer)
blocos.conteudo:
ROLE: You are a directing assistant and you write video prompts for generators with audio.
INPUT: a storyboard (one line per shot), a lookbook, and a list of references, pasted at the end.
OUTPUT: first the lines "Scene:", "Base prompt:" and "Lock:"; then one line per shot, in this format:
n | duration | shot size | movement | prompt: <camera, subject, action, setting> | sound: <ambience, effect, dialogue as someone saying: text>
VOCABULARY: size, angle, and movement only with the terms from the storyboard (wide shot, close-up, high camera, dolly in, static camera...).
RULES:
- copy the Base prompt from the lookbook and the Lock from the references word for word;
- one movement per shot, the same as in the storyboard;
- sound in its own sentence, after "sound:";
- do not mention a director, film, brand, or real person.
LIMITS: do not invent a character, place, object, or line of dialogue that is not in the input. If something is missing, write "MISSING:" and what was missing.
Storyboard:
<paste the storyboard.txt here>
Lookbook:
<paste the lookbook.txt here>
References:
<paste the referencias.txt here>

Scene: <name> (<duration> s)
Base prompt: <from lookbook.txt, word for word>
Lock: <from referencias.txt, word for word>
<n> | <n> s | <shot size> | <one movement> | prompt: <camera, subject, action, setting> | sound: <ambience, effect, dialogue>

txt.titulo: Plan — Generation: AI image and video
txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

perguntas.p: Which layer of the request does the most to keep the assistant from making things up?
opcoes: The role, because it defines who the assistant is.
The vocabulary, because it limits the camera words.
The output format, because it fixes exactly the line each shot has to follow.
The limits, which say to write "FALTA:" instead of making things up.
perguntas.explica: If you don't say what to do when information is missing, the assistant fills the gap with something plausible. With "FALTA:", the gap shows up so you can decide.

perguntas.p: The list passed the page's check, but shot 3 has a grandson of Dona Lia who isn't in the storyboard. What do you do?
opcoes: Take the grandson out of the line and add a rule to the request.
Keep it, because the page accepted the list.
Switch to another AI assistant and ask again.
Delete all of shot 3 from the list.
perguntas.explica: The page checks format and numbers, not content. Made-up details get fixed in the line and become a rule in the request, so they don't come back in the next storyboard.

perguntas.p: Why copy the base prompt and the lock word for word into every line?
opcoes: Because the generator only accepts prompts of the same length.
Because the same text asks for the same look and the same character.
Because the page only checks lines that match each other.
That way the assistant uses less of your subscription.
perguntas.explica: It's the continuity from lessons 3 and 5, carried over into the list: whatever must be the same in every shot goes in the same. Only the camera, the action, and the sound change from line to line.

perguntas.p: The generator you were using shut down. What do you need to redo?
opcoes: Everything, starting from the storyboard from course 0.
The stills and the references, which got stuck inside the platform that shut down.
Only the generations: the list, lookbook, and references are in your folder.
The prompt list, because each generator has its own format.
perguntas.explica: That's why everything is a text and image file in your folder, outside the platform: it's what the Sora case taught. Adjusting how you write for another generator is small next to redoing the scene.

itens.texto: Role, input, output, vocabulary, rules, and limits; the request can be reused.
The page checks the format; you check for made-up details and turn each one into a rule.
Base prompt, lock, and one line per shot, ready for any generator.
